htmlMeta: Plan {name} · base {base} · commit {commit} · updated {date}. The JSON twin is for agents; this page is generated from it.
htmlInstructions: Protocol for every agent: the tracker block of {files}. One lot at a time: {cli} lot take <id|next> --agent <name> --wait.
htmlConflictsIntro: These lots cite the same files: fix them one after the other.
instrIntro: A plan in `{dir}/` (`<name>.json` for an agent, `<name>.html` for a reader) cuts the open issues into numbered lots. This protocol holds for every plan and every agent — Claude Code, Codex, a shell. It is written by the tracker plugin (`instructions`): change the plugin, not this block.
instr_1: **Change nothing — neither the repository nor GitHub — until a lot is named.** A lot with a `done` field is finished: do not take it again; `done.pr.state` at `draft` means its pull request is still to merge.
instr_2: **One lot at a time, whatever the agent**: before any change, `{cli} lot take <id|next> --agent <name> --wait`. Exit `0`: the lock is yours. **`75`: another lot is in progress — run the same command again until it exits `0`, and touch nothing meanwhile**; after waiting, it means “still busy”, not “failed”. `2`: no such lot, or already done. `{cli} lot lock` says who holds it, `{cli} lot status` lists the lots.
instr_3: **A `fix/` branch from `{base}`**, one commit per issue ending with `Closes #<n>`, the project’s checks, then a **draft** pull request. In Claude Code, `/tracker:lot <id|next>` does all of it.
instr_4: **Re-measure before fixing**: each issue names its report, its run and its key — read the report and check the defect at the latest commit. `codeFix: false` means a setting or a database state, not a diff; `awaitDeploy: true`, only after the deployment it names; `bag: true`, split the issue first; the lots listed in `conflicts` cite the same files.
instr_5: **End of a lot**: `{cli} lot mark <id> --pr <n> [--state draft|merged]` updates the JSON **and** the HTML **and releases the lock** (`/tracker:lot` does it when it opens the pull request). A lot given up: `{cli} lot release <id>`.
instr_6: **The plan is committed on `{base}`, never on the lot’s branch** — each fix branch would conflict with the next one when merged: `{cli} lot commit`. `{cli} lot sync --apply` records the merged pull requests.
instrLock: ⚠️ The lock lives in git’s common directory (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`): shared by every worktree of the clone, never committed, taken atomically. `--wait` gives up after a few minutes, below the 10-minute limit of the agents’ shell tools. A lock not renewed for a few hours goes stale and another agent may take it: an agent that died in a lot does not block the others.
